workout.warmup: Your 15-min walk to the gym is your warmup. DO ramp-up sets on the Smith bench (a light 8, then a medium 5) before heavy work.
workout.coach_note: Swapped from lower to upper — you ran 5.75 hilly miles Thursday (Phinney Ridge) and have a big walk Friday, so legs get the weekend off and LOWER moves to Monday. Downhill running is eccentric and hits quads hard 24-48h later; no point grinding a heavy leg day on that. Main lifts heavy 4x5-6 with 2-3 min rest, accessories 10-15. Progressions are off your strong 7/15 session. Ballard Smith bar = 25 lb, factor that in.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Bench Press [HEAVY]
exercises.note: MAIN LIFT. You owned 165 total (70/side + 25 bar) for a clean 4x5 on 7/15. Add 5 lb per side = 175 total, aim 4x5. If you stall at 3 reps, drop back to 165 and get 4x6. Ramp up first — don't jump straight to the working weight like last time.

exercises.name: DB Shoulder Press [HEAVY]
exercises.note: MAIN LIFT. 55s gave you 6/5/6 last time — own all sets at 6 before going up. Watch the left shoulder; stop a rep short rather than grind.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row [HEAVY]
exercises.note: MAIN LIFT. 150 for 4x6 moved well on 7/15 — go to 155–160. Your pulls are your strongest lift right now. Chest up, no jerking.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown [HEAVY]
exercises.note: MAIN LIFT. 145 for 4x6 was clean — bump to 150–155. Neutral grip if available. Full stretch at the top, drive elbows down.

exercises.name: Face Pulls
exercises.note: Accessory, stays high-rep. Gauge the Ballard machine by feel — the number didn't match other locations. Elbows high and wide. Pairs well with your band rehab.

exercises.name: Arms Superset — Rope Pushdown + Hammer Curl
exercises.note: Accessories stay 10–15 through the block. Both moved for 12s on 7/15 — hold, add reps or a little weight if easy.

exercises.name: Core Circuit (fresh combo) — 2 rounds
exercises.detail: Cable Crunch x12 → Bicycle Crunch x24 → Side Plank 45–60s/side
exercises.note: Different from your last two circuits. Side planks at 45–60s per your own read — you're holding a minute comfortably now.
